newsitem.title: JAPAN: Two key Japan cult suspects turn themselves in.
newsitem.headline: Two key Japan cult suspects turn themselves in.

text.p: Two of the most wanted members of the Japanese doomsday cult accused of last year's Tokyo subway gas attack came out of hiding on Thursday and gave themselves up after 18 months on the run.

Koichi Kitamura and Zenji Yagisawa were among the seven key suspect members of the Aum Shinri Kyo (Supreme Truth Sect) whose "wanted" portraits have been posted all over the country in a relentless police campaign to track them down.
Police say Kitamura, 28, was part of the 10-member team which carried out the attack on the Tokyo subway system on March 20, 1995.
Twelve people died and 6,000 people were made ill when sarin nerve gas was released on five trains by puncturing plastic bags containing the gas with the sharpened tips of umbrellas.

Police have identified Yagisawa, 34, as the key suspect in an attempted cyanide gassing of an underground shopping mall in Shinjuku, a prime shopping and entertainment district in Tokyo, on May 5, 1995.
Police allege Yagisawa placed a crude device designed to release cyanide gas in a toilet in the mall, but a cleaner found the device and police defused it before it went off.
At the time, police said that if the attack had succeeded, it could have killed thousands of people in the mall, which had been crowded because the day was a national holiday.
A police spokesman said Yagisawa turned himself in by suddenly appearing at the Tokorozawa police station in Saitama prefecture adjacent to Tokyo, on Thursday morning.
He carried a copy of the "wanted" poster, pointed to it and said simply: "I am too tired."
Yagisawa led police to an apartment he was sharing with Kitamura, who turned himself in as soon as police knocked at the door and revealed who they were.
Police said the two would be closely questioned about the other five key suspects still at large.
Cult guru Shoko Asahara is now on trial for murder in the subway attack and a host of other alleged cases, including other gas attacks, kidnappings and murders.
Asahara has not entered a plea. The maximum penalty for murder is death by hanging.
Recently, Asahara has gone into fits of uncontrolled rage during his trial at the Tokyo District Court when key disciples gave evidence against him.
More that 100 other cult members are also on trial in connection with the sect's activities.
